_comment: Machine-readable mirror of openstudio-necb/docs/necb_decisions.md — the adjudicated
interpretations and product decisions governing the NECB Part 8 pipeline. Runtime code
cites these ids through the AuditLog `ruling:` kwarg, and the AHJ report's rulings
appendix renders the ones that actually fired in a run, so a reader sees WHY a value was
chosen without needing access to this repository's documentation.
kind: runtime          — governs a code path that carries a `ruling:` audit tag
runtime_unwired  — governs runtime behaviour with no ruling-tagged audit call
data             — manifest / vendored-data or verification-only decision
process          — how the project works (authorship, delegation, sign-off, sweeps)
MAINTENANCE: every `## D-XX` heading in necb_decisions.md must have an entry here, and
every kind:runtime entry must be cited by at least one `ruling:` literal in gem code.
Summaries are PARAPHRASE — never reproduce NECB text verbatim here (D-01 governs where
code text may be reproduced, and this file is not one of those places).

decisions.title: NECB text reproduction (Crown copyright)
decisions.summary: Generated coverage documents committed to the public repository may quote NECB article text in full, because NRCan is the Crown and the code's copyright belongs to the Government of Canada. This decision scopes where verbatim code text is allowed: the generated coverage HTML and its article cache, not arbitrary source or data files.

decisions.title: Unresolvable space types are a hard error
decisions.summary: Before running a performance-path determination the pipeline checks every floor-area space type against the NECB catalog and raises an error (with did-you-mean suggestions) when one cannot be resolved. The earlier behaviour silently waived the lighting allowance for unmatched types, producing a compliance result that looked complete but was not. This is deliberately breaking for untagged models.

decisions.title: Chiller EIR curves verified against the proposed erratum
decisions.summary: Two water-cooled chiller part-load rows in the printed tables carry misplaced decimals — one yields a physically impossible negative power ratio at the rating point. The verification probe therefore compares against erratum-corrected coefficients, labelled as such pending NRC confirmation, since an independent vendored curve lineage corroborates the corrections to within a few parts per million.

decisions.title: EUI path: two-run design with check-then-normalize
decisions.summary: The archetype-EUI path and the reference-performance path evaluate different proposed models, so normalization to the archetype operating-condition table uses a two-run design: first check whether the model already carries the table values, and only run a second annual simulation if it does not. By default the EUI supplement reports NOT COMPUTED with the mismatches listed rather than silently doubling simulation cost; an explicit opt-in runs the normalized model.

decisions.title: Two archetype-normalization interpretations adopted
decisions.summary: Two readings of the archetype operating-conditions table were adopted: lighting operating schedules are normalized (not only lighting power density), and outdoor-air rates are taken as the applicable ventilation standard's rates evaluated at the table's occupant density. Leaving the proposed model's lighting schedules or ventilation rates in place would leak design-specific behaviour into a run whose whole purpose is an apples-to-apples archetype comparison.

decisions.title: Energy-recovery trigger uses the current-vintage airflow tables, post-sizing
decisions.summary: The inherited energy-recovery trigger was a much older vintage's exhaust-heat-content formula, which is permissive for small high-outdoor-air systems. It was replaced with the current editions' airflow-threshold tables — heating-degree-day row by percent-outdoor-air band, split by whether the system operates continuously — evaluated after sizing, since the thresholds cannot be known before flows exist. Sizing-only and no-simulation modes skip the determination loudly rather than guessing.

decisions.title: Cooling-tower part-load behaviour dispositioned to the engine
decisions.summary: The reference tower's part-load capacity requirement is satisfied by EnergyPlus's effectiveness-NTU tower model, which exposes no curve fields the code's polynomial could be installed into. The disposition is backed by a gated numeric cross-check rather than argument alone: exact agreement at the industry rating point and bounded divergence across the rating slice, in the conservative direction at cold wet-bulbs where capacity never binds.

decisions.title: Batch sign-off of the remaining article dispositions
decisions.summary: The nineteen remaining draft article dispositions were signed off in four groups: probe-evidenced coverage claims, engine-physics claims, modeller-responsibility articles, and four acknowledged gaps that stay publicly documented as uncovered. A disposition is a claim of responsibility rather than of correctness — the deliberately weaker claim — so implementing any of the gap articles later remains separate, evidence-backed work.

decisions.title: Umbrella coverage manifest emits at runtime; modeller-scope notes split from warnings
decisions.summary: The umbrella gem emits its own article-coverage manifest into the audit at the end of every successful run, and all six emitters share one semantic: a partial or unimplemented entry whose remaining gap is wholly the modeller's responsibility emits as an informational scope note rather than a warning. A warning no model change can ever clear trains readers to ignore warnings altogether. Its audit calls are the coverage emitters, which are deliberately left untagged so the report's fired-rulings counts reflect real code paths rather than manifest boilerplate.

decisions.title: Remaining adjudications delegated, with mandatory logging
decisions.summary: The project owner delegated the remaining queued interpretation decisions, on the condition that every judgement call is logged as a numbered decision entry, self-contained enough to be reversed on later review. Entries marked as made under this delegation were decided on the best evidence-backed recommendation rather than by direct instruction.

decisions.title: Hydronic pump power implemented as intensity transfer plus table curves
decisions.summary: Reference hydronic pump power is derived from the proposed building's combined pump power intensity in watts per litre per second, matched by loop type rather than pump-to-pump, since the two buildings' topologies legitimately differ. The intensity is multiplied by the reference's own flow rather than transferred as absolute watts, which prevents a consolidation free ride. Variable-speed reference pumps additionally receive the table's riding-curve coefficients with a minimum-flow clamp.

decisions.title: Space temperature control re-manifested as modeller scope
decisions.summary: Claiming this article unimplemented was factually wrong. Identical throttling between the two buildings is satisfied by construction, because both use ideal thermostat control on cloned schedules with no throttling knob that could differ. The remaining sentence only binds when a modeller approximates a radiant design convectively, which is the modeller's responsibility, so the entry is now a scope note rather than a permanent warning.

decisions.title: Screw and centrifugal chiller curves probed; imperfect printed normalization accepted
decisions.summary: The water-cooled screw and centrifugal curve rows match the printed tables exactly and are not erratum-affected. Three of those printed fits do not normalize to unity at the standard rating point; this is accepted as a genuine property of the published curve fits rather than a transcription error, because an independent vendored curve lineage agrees with the printed rows digit for digit.

decisions.title: Reference air systems inherit the proposed operating schedule
decisions.summary: Each zone's proposed air-system availability schedule is captured before the HVAC strip and applied to the reference loop serving those zones, since operating schedules must be identical in both buildings. With no proposed air system the builder default is retained with an informational note; when one reference loop's zones carried conflicting schedules the most-common one wins with a loud warning. This also feeds the energy-recovery continuous-versus-intermittent classification.

decisions.title: Energy-recovery effectiveness and frost values verified against the code text
decisions.summary: The minimum effectiveness requirement is enthalpy-based, and setting both sensible and latent effectiveness to the minimum yields exactly that enthalpy effectiveness by identity — minimum-compliant for a reference build, verified on every heat-exchanger field. The overshoot-control requirement is met by supply-air outlet temperature control plus a pretreat setpoint manager. The frost-control values are simulation-engine modelling assumptions, not code values, and are now labelled as such so they cannot be mistaken for code transcriptions.

decisions.title: Orphaned proposed EMS purged from the reference
decisions.summary: An archetype breadth sweep found that some proposed models' energy-management-system programs survive the reference HVAC strip carrying dangling object references, which reach the simulation engine as raw identifier tokens and cause a fatal error. Such programs, along with emptied calling managers and orphaned actuators, are now removed with a loud audit warning: the reference building's controls come from the reference ruleset, never from proposed-side overrides.

decisions.title: Legacy energy-recovery diagnosis filed upstream
decisions.summary: The legacy library's energy-recovery determination was diagnosed to file and line and reported upstream: its newest applicable vintage inherits an older data-driven formula that transcribes only the continuous-operation table, so it never consults operating hours and has no low-outdoor-air exemption. The result is over-equipping recovery devices above the heating-degree-day threshold, observed on several archetypes. The issue includes a full solution draft and regression tests.

decisions.title: Multizone system zone grouping rewritten to the table note
decisions.summary: The builder's one-air-handler-per-storey convention had no code basis and was caught by an archetype comparison in which our reference built ten corridor systems where the legacy library built one. Grouping now follows the table note literally: one system for all storeys up to four above grade, and above that external thermal blocks grouped by facade orientation with internal and underground blocks in their own groups. Corner blocks bin by largest exterior wall area with a deterministic tie-break.

decisions.title: Infiltration lineage reconciled; reference inherits proposed leakage coefficients
decisions.summary: For an untested building the proposed and reference must carry identical air leakage, so an observed large difference was not code-intended. The real defect was ours and temporal: the reference wrote a constant-coefficient infiltration convention while the cloned proposed carried wind-driven coefficients, giving identical design totals but very different delivered air changes. The reference now inherits the proposed's coefficients and schedule, and a proposed whose installed total deviates materially from the code default draws a loud warning.

decisions.title: Economizer exempted on 100%-outdoor-air makeup air units
decisions.summary: A residual reference heating gap was traced to the economizer pass applying differential-enthalpy control to every reference air system, including a fully outdoor-air makeup air unit. Such a system cannot economize, but the winter economizer signal engages the heat-exchanger lockout and bypasses the mandated energy-recovery wheel for the entire heating season. The pass now exempts these systems with an audited note, which brought reference heating into agreement with the proposed.

decisions.title: Envelope area for air leakage computed as the conditioned-space enclosure
decisions.summary: The normalization area for default air leakage is the set of surfaces separating conditioned from unconditioned space. For an unconditioned attic that means the ceiling below it counts and the attic roof does not — both our implementation and the legacy library had been computing a roof-inclusive area, a shared conservative bias. The area is now built as the enclosure of the conditioned volume, and unconditioned spaces receive no infiltration object at all.

decisions.title: Reference-systems audit findings implemented as one batch
decisions.summary: Thirteen findings from a four-way reference-systems audit were fixed together: oversizing caps made to actually bind, heat-rejection fan power corrected to the current table value, the economizer applicability trigger evaluated after sizing, heat-pump heating capacity pinned to cooling capacity, night-cycle and minimum-outdoor-air scheduling added, energy-recovery wheel parasitic power modelled, zone-equipment fans brought to the reference fan specification, and several warnings added where the pipeline had been silent. The archetype fleet converged to the tightest fixed-point clustering achieved so far.

decisions.title: Table transmittance values treated as overall, air films included
decisions.summary: An object-level comparison against legacy archetypes showed every wall differing by about four percent. The code's own definition settles it: overall thermal transmittance accounts for the air films on both faces, so the prescriptive table values include films and the construction-only conductance must be derived by subtracting them. The film-inclusive convention is now the default, with simple-glazing fenestration exempt because its rated factor is already the film-inclusive value.

decisions.title: Envelope scope: unconditioned spaces out, interzone assemblies in
decisions.summary: Both the prescriptive and reference envelope transforms had been iterating all exterior and ground surfaces while skipping all interzone surfaces, which is backwards relative to the definition of the building envelope as what separates conditioned space from everything else. Surfaces belonging to unconditioned spaces are now left untouched with an audited note, while assemblies separating conditioned from enclosed unconditioned space are treated as envelope, with the table row chosen by inclination and the enclosure credited.

decisions.title: Design-day attach replaces rather than appends, filtered to annual extremes
decisions.summary: A cooling-tower archetype crashed during sizing because the weather-attach step appended a full design-day file onto models that already carried design days, and a first-cut filter still matched monthly percentile days whose low wet-bulbs make the tower heat-transfer solve infeasible. The attach step now removes existing design days and imports only the small standard extreme set, falling back to the full set only when nothing matches.

decisions.title: Heat-rejection fan power sums the condenser loop; sized tower hydraulics hardened
decisions.summary: Tower fan power had been computed from a single chiller, so a two-chiller plant produced half the required value; heat rejection is now summed across all chillers on the loop after their capacities are final. Separately, re-running sizing with a hard-set code fan power can make the engine's tower heat-transfer solve fail, so the pass first freezes the previously solved flow and heat-transfer values — the code governs fan power, not the tower's heat-transfer sizing.

decisions.title: Service-water circulators are outside the hydronic pump article; transfer head reconciled
decisions.summary: The pump-power transfer had been applying a space-heating power intensity to service-water circulators, which combined with an inherited high head implies an impossible pump efficiency and is fatal to the simulation engine. Loops carrying a water heater or water-use connections are now outside the hydronic pump scope entirely, and are also excluded from the proposed-side intensity statistics. Every remaining transfer carries a physicality guard that reconciles head, with a loud warning, when the implied efficiency is impossible.

decisions.title: Multizone selection groups merge into whole-building systems
decisions.summary: Because a proposed archetype may partition its zones per storey, building one reference system per selection group leaked that partition into the reference and produced far more systems than the table note prescribes. The fragmentation had real consequences: small per-loop flows fell below the economizer and energy-recovery thresholds. Multizone build assignments of the same catalog family now merge before building, with the facade and internal split happening inside the builder; single-zone families keep their selection grouping.

decisions.title: Upstream issues carry explicit Claude authorship
decisions.summary: At the project owner's direction, upstream issues drafted by the AI assistant state that authorship in the issue body, even when submitted from a human account for access reasons. The note was also applied retroactively to previously filed issues. This is a standing rule for future filings and supersedes an earlier no-attribution convention.

decisions.title: Legacy findings ledger cleared upstream
decisions.summary: Eight legacy-library findings were filed upstream as three grouped issues covering reference-system selection, reference modelling rules, and a construction film-convention disagreement. After this the ledger had no unfiled rows, leaving only entries that were still under investigation.

decisions.title: Two legacy findings root-caused and closed with no defect
decisions.summary: A suspected cooling-efficiency mismatch turned out to be a false premise: the archetype coil names carry ratings that are exactly the printed minimums, and the observed coefficients follow from the standard fan-stripping conversions, which are identical in both lineages. A suspected wrong-vintage energy-recovery trigger was found to be vintage-correct for that edition. The convention that rated efficiencies are fan-inclusive while engine coil coefficients are coil-only is now pinned.

decisions.title: Ground-floor insulation extent corrected to a perimeter strip below the coldest zone
decisions.summary: A warehouse residual was traced to insulating the full slab area to the table value in climate zones where the printed table prescribes only a perimeter strip and sets no maximum for the slab field. The transform now keeps the modelled slab field in those zones and adds the strip via the foundation model's interior horizontal insulation, sized so the strip assembly meets the table value; the coldest zone keeps its full-area requirement. Ground floors without a foundation object get an audited warning that the strip is not representable.

decisions.title: Variant mockups exercise the never-fleet-tested reference routes
decisions.summary: A coverage audit showed the archetype fleet only ever selects a handful of reference system types, leaving several build routes never exercised end to end. Seven synthetic mockup models were generated so that every reference route runs through the full pipeline including sizing. This also surfaced a space-type keyword-ordering collision affecting museum exhibition areas, queued for adjudication.

decisions.title: Residential blocks with heat pumps take the air-source redirect
decisions.summary: A residential or accommodation block whose proposed system includes a heat pump takes the air-source heat-pump reference redirect rather than the selection table's identical-to-proposed parenthetical. The ruling was to follow the legacy library's effective behaviour, which has no per-block heat-pump detection and redirects whenever heat pumps are present anywhere. The heat-pump check therefore runs before the other residential branches.

decisions.title: Lightweight reference rebuild corrected to light-frame mass
decisions.summary: The explanatory note for the thermal-mass requirement makes clear that lightweight does not mean massless: it directs following the proposed assembly's layer structure with insulation varied to meet the required transmittance, and its example assemblies are light-frame constructions with real areal mass and heat capacity. Opaque reference assemblies are now rebuilt with a single calibrated material carrying the note's wood-frame example properties instead of a massless layer, which also lets one material serve every boundary condition.

decisions.title: Campus 3D renderer ported into the geometry gem
decisions.summary: A model viewer from a separate campus project was ported into the geometry gem at the project owner's request, keeping the original design: a crash-isolated subprocess export, a three-step repair ladder that falls back to a massing shell and then bisects out crashing surfaces, and a self-contained embedded viewer page. It is a visualization utility with no bearing on compliance determination.

decisions.title: Heat-pump reference split by source, boundary per the explanatory note
decisions.summary: Heat pumps on an internal water loop — the configuration the explanatory note describes, where an auxiliary boiler and heat-rejection device are expressly allowed — keep their ordinary selection-table reference. Air-, water- and ground-source heat pumps redirect to the air-source heat-pump reference instead. Each group's heat-pump sources are classified from the source plant loop, and a detected heat pump with no source evidence keeps the conservative redirect.

decisions.title: Prescriptive pump-power caps applied min-wins over the intensity transfer
decisions.summary: Reference hydronic pump power is set by the proposed-intensity transfer and then clamped at the prescriptive maximum watts per kilowatt of the loop's peak thermal demand, because the prescriptive requirement is a ceiling the reference building may never pierce. Taking the smaller of the two is the only reading that satisfies both articles at once, and it removes the perverse incentive whereby wasteful proposed pumping inflates its own target. Unsized inputs produce an audited not-evaluable note rather than a silent skip.

decisions.title: Two-pipe fan-coil reference heating honoured conditionally
decisions.summary: The selection table lists this reference system with no heating, while a separate sentence requires heating presence per thermal block to match the proposed. The reconciliation: a cooled-but-unheated proposed block gets the table-literal cooling-only reference, and a heated block keeps the existing two-pipe changeover heating under the presence override, with no new heating equipment invented. A block with no conditioning at all still gets no reference system, since that is absence rather than a stated none.

decisions.title: Reheat-coil autosizing trusted; legacy hard-size workaround rejected
decisions.summary: Reference variable-air-volume reheat coils stay autosized; the legacy library's geometry-based hard-sizing formula was measured against a sized reference building and misses in both directions by up to an order of magnitude because it is load-blind. Adopting it would undersize some coils, inflate others into the plant sizing, disable the capacity auto-iteration that hard-sized equipment ignores, and rests on no code text.

decisions.title: Service-water reference article machine-verified; gap refined
decisions.summary: The service-water manifest's long-standing caveat that the article text was not machine-verifiable is closed now that the full article and its explanatory note retrieve cleanly. The verification showed the clone-based treatment already satisfies most sentences, so the declared gap was narrowed to two genuinely unimplemented items: part-load curves on reference service-water equipment, and consolidation of multiple proposed circulation pumps into one.

decisions.title: First full-annual fleet sweep validates reference generation
decisions.summary: The first code-compliant-duration sweep across fifteen archetypes put thirteen of them within a narrow band of the fixed-point expectation, and showed reference conditioning is sound through a full year with essentially no unmet heating hours. The non-compliance wave came from the proposed side: the legacy archetypes' hard-sized cooling produces far more unmet cooling hours than the reference, and hard-sized equipment does not respond to sizing-factor iteration. The reference pipeline itself behaved correctly end to end.

decisions.title: Capacity iteration made per thermal block, secant-targeted from run history
decisions.summary: The capacity auto-iteration no longer bumps only the building's global sizing factors. Each round reads the previous annual run's per-zone unmet-hours and raises sizing factors on the failing thermal blocks only, which is the code-literal reading since the governing sentences are written per thermal block. The first bump per zone is geometric and later bumps are extrapolated from that zone's own history, clamped so the increase stays incremental; global and mixed fallbacks are audited by name.

decisions.title: Decision rulings surfaced at runtime in the audit log and AHJ report
decisions.summary: Adjudicated decisions previously lived only in project documentation, so a user running the pipeline never learned why a ruled code path behaved as it did. Audit entries now carry an optional ruling tag citing decision identifiers alongside the existing code-article citation, this registry mirrors every decision in machine-readable form with a self-contained summary, and the compliance report renders an appendix listing the decisions that actually fired in the run. Purely additive: no determination behaviour changes.

decisions.title: Museum exhibition galleries take the assembly row; museum archives and restoration rooms take the collections row
decisions.summary: A museum space can match two rows of the reference-system selection table, and the matcher takes the first keyword hit, so the answer depended on the order the categories sat in the data file. The collections row names the archives of museums and galleries rather than museums generally, and the assembly row explicitly lists exhibit space, so a public exhibition gallery takes the assembly row while archives and restoration rooms take the collections row. The over-broad museum keyword was narrowed so each space matches on intent rather than scan position.

decisions.title: Staged heating and cooling as unitary multispeed coils, stage count set after sizing
decisions.summary: The code requires the reference building's furnaces and direct-expansion systems to be modelled as equal capacity stages, two of them up to a threshold capacity and one per threshold increment above it. Reference packaged single-zone systems now build their fan and coils inside a unitary container holding multi-stage coils, because the simulation engine cannot place a multi-stage coil directly on an air loop; a pass that runs after sizing sets only the NUMBER of stages from the sized total, leaving every stage capacity automatically sized so that capacity auto-iteration keeps working. Equal increments are realized through the container's per-stage airflow ratios, and minimum-efficiency values are looked up once against the unit's total capacity and written to every stage.

decisions.title: Stage count clamped at the simulation engine's four-stage ceiling, with a shouted warning
decisions.summary: The multi-stage coil objects in the simulation engine cannot hold more than four stages, so very large equipment cannot be given the number of equal stages the code asks for. The stage count is clamped at four and every clamp raises a loud audit warning naming the required count, the sized capacity and the ceiling, so that oversized cases are enumerated rather than hidden. Splitting the load across extra parallel units was rejected because it would change the reference system topology to work around a tool limit.

decisions.title: Staging applies to air-loop unitary equipment only; zone terminals and tempering coils stay single-speed
decisions.summary: Equipment staging is applied to air-loop unitary equipment only. Packaged terminal units keep single-speed coils because the simulation engine's input schema forbids a multi-stage coil there even though the modelling toolkit accepts the assignment, and make-up-air tempering coils temper a ventilation stream rather than being the staged unitary equipment the sentences describe. Every skip is reported in the audit grouped by reason with a count, rather than one entry per coil, so that a building with hundreds of identical terminals does not swamp the report.

decisions.title: Electric resistance heating is not a furnace, so the furnace staging sentence does not reach it
decisions.summary: The staging sentence governs furnaces, and an electric resistance heating coil is not one: it has no burner, no combustion staging, and linear part-load behaviour, so dividing it into equal stages would add objects without changing anything physical. Electric-heated reference packaged systems therefore pair the staged multi-speed cooling coil, which the cooling article does require, with a plain single-stage electric heating coil in the same unitary container.

decisions.title: Terminal and secondary capacity split accounted through dedicated-outdoor-air zone sizing
decisions.summary: Where the selection table places heating or cooling in both a zone terminal and a secondary system, the terminal is to be sized for the space loads while the pair together covers the peak. For the reference systems that pair a zone terminal with a make-up-air unit this is expressed directly as dedicated-outdoor-air zone-sizing accounting with a neutral supply-air strategy, so the ventilation stream neither adds nor removes zone load and the terminal is sized on the space load alone. Reference systems that mix outdoor air into the supply stream have no equivalent accounting, so their split is only approximated by ordinary mixed-air zone sizing and each such group is audited as an approximation.

decisions.title: Reference daylighting photocontrols are built by default
decisions.summary: The reference building is required to carry the daylighting photocontrols that the prescriptive lighting-control requirements mandate, and the effect of those controls must be evaluated in the reference. The pipeline therefore builds them on every reference-path run by default and evaluates them with detailed daylighting calculations, because a reference generated without them over-states reference lighting energy and hands the proposed building an energy target more lenient than the code sets. A caller may still switch the photocontrols off, and a run that does so is warned in the audit that the requirement went unevaluated rather than being left silent.

decisions.title: The reference heat pump's auxiliary-heating energy type is elected from the proposed building's annual run
decisions.summary: The heat-pump reference system's terminal or auxiliary heating must take the energy type used for terminal or auxiliary heating of the thermal blocks the heat pump serves that has the largest annual energy use, provided the heat pump itself carries more than a third of those blocks' total annual space-heating energy. That is an annual-energy question, so the proposed building's annual simulation is now run BEFORE the reference is built - it depends on nothing downstream, so the reordering costs no additional simulation - and its per-equipment delivered heating energy is aggregated by energy type over the blocks each heat pump serves: the pump's own blocks for an air-source machine, the blocks of every pump sharing the same source water loop for a water- or ground-source machine. All quantities compared are delivered heat, one consistent basis across energy types. Where the election cannot run - no annual data because only sizing was requested, blocks with no terminal or auxiliary heating at all, or a heat-pump share at or below the threshold so the sentence's proviso is unmet - the structural energy-type proxy that follows the proposed system's fuels elects instead, and the audit states plainly which path elected the fuel. The election is made once, from the first annual run, and is not re-litigated by later capacity iterations, which adjust sizes but never rebuild the reference topology. The clause forcing electricity for a pump that is neither air-, water- nor ground-source is only applied when such a source is affirmatively established, which the current source taxonomy never produces, so an evidence-less detection keeps the proxy rather than guessing. The cooling-capacity clause - peak cooling load without oversizing - was verified by measurement rather than assumption: the per-zone unit cooling sizing factor the heat-pump builders stamp overrides the model-wide capped factor, giving identical sized capacity with the global factor at its cap versus at unity.

decisions.title: Staleness audit after the extraction-service fixes: every pre-fix vendored table re-verified against the corrected source
decisions.summary: The table-extraction service behind the code data was fixed in four stages after most of the vendored data had been transcribed, so every vendored artifact whose primary source was the extraction service - rather than the legacy implementation - was re-fetched against the corrected extraction and diffed value by value: the lighting power densities, the energy-recovery thresholds, the pump power-curve coefficients and pumping-power caps, the envelope thermal-transmittance ladders including the perimeter-strip ground-floor nuance, the exterior lighting allowances, the greenhouse-gas performance levels and provincial emission factors, and the archetype energy-use-intensity targets. Every value matches the corrected printed tables exactly, and the part-load-curve probe re-run confirms the curve equations verified during the window when equations could be attached to the wrong article still hold. Zero stale-data defects were found, for structural reasons worth keeping: the corruption was concentrated in complex multi-header tables and in cross-table letter alignment - both already caught and corrected by earlier decisions - while the numeric single-header tables extracted correctly even before the fixes; several files were cross-checked against the legacy implementation at build time; and the name-keyed joins used for the lighting data fail loudly on row misalignment rather than silently shifting values. The re-verified files carry a dated stamp in their provenance blocks so the next extraction-service fix has a clear audit trail of what was checked against which state of the source.

decisions.title: The Hospital reference's slow annual run is the ventilation floor meeting the per-stage flow band, plus thirty required energy-recovery wheels - inherent cost, one small lead left open
decisions.summary: The reference annual run for the largest archetype takes three to four times its proposed's runtime, with tens of millions of recurring warnings. Root-caused on two axes. The warning churn is the staged cooling coils' lowest stages operating above the simulator's flow-per-watt band on high-outdoor-air hospital loops: the staged supply flow is deliberately floored at the minimum outdoor-air fraction so staging can never starve ventilation, and on loops whose ventilation fraction exceeds the lowest stage's capacity fraction that floor sits outside the band, so the simulator warns and clamps at every call - verified by the converse, a low-outdoor-air staged model with an economizer logging zero such warnings. Abandoning the floor would trade a warning for a ventilation violation, so the churn is dispositioned as inherent. The runtime delta is substantially legitimate equipment: the reference carries thirty energy-recovery wheels the legacy proposed lacks because the code requires them, each simulated every timestep. One lead stays open: four input-time severe errors about unbalanced air volume flow on two nurses-station energy-recovery wheels - localized, non-fatal, and worth a targeted flow-balance look when that subsystem is next touched. Practical consequence recorded: the two largest archetypes need a twelve-hour window for full-annual sweeps.

decisions.title: The SmallHotel reference's unmet-heating gate failure is morning setback-recovery lag in four micro-zones - a characteristic, not a build defect
decisions.summary: The reference building's persistent unmet-heating hours on this archetype were traced to exactly four storage closets under five square metres, one per storey, served by one shared constant-volume system with autosized electric baseboards. The hours accumulate as roughly half an hour to an hour of morning setback recovery every day of the year: an honestly autosized baseboard in a tiny zone recovers the overnight setback slowly, the sentence-five capacity increase raises the zone sizing factors to two and three times but each round shaves less than an hour so the stall detector halts, and the proposed building masks the identical physics because the legacy generator hard-sizes its equipment generously. Remediation options - splitting the shared single-zone system per thermal block, which the industrial-row note points the OPPOSITE way on since it says the reference may be divided only to match the proposed's units; an oversizing floor for micro-zones; or aligning the recovery ramp - are all design decisions that would move the reference away from plain autosizing, so the failure is dispositioned as a characteristic of the corrected reference against hard-sized legacy proposeds and left standing in the baseline table rather than engineered away.

decisions.title: Pool-heater and solar-thermal service-water minimums applied when present, from the printed rows the extraction lost
decisions.summary: The service-water-heater performance table's solar-thermal and pool-heater sections were lost from the code extraction in both editions, so the reference pipeline could never have applied them and the gap was declared rather than closed. The printed minimums were recovered by the extraction service's own page-verified audit and are now vendored and applied when the equipment is present: a water heater serving an indoor swimming pool is set to the printed minimum thermal efficiency for its fuel, a heat-pump pool heater is floored at the printed coefficient of performance, and fuels with no printed pool row are left as cloned with a note rather than forced. The solar-thermal minimum is a Solar Energy Factor - an equipment rating with no corresponding simulation input - so detected solar collectors receive an audited determination citing the printed values while their physics remain as cloned, never a silent skip. No archetype carries either equipment class, so the pass is a structural no-op on the fleet, proven by a control run; it exists for foreign proposed buildings.

decisions.title: Economizer systems' staged cooling gets the prescribed lowest-stage capacity floor
decisions.summary: Air-economizer systems must incorporate cooling equipment that can operate below full capacity, with the lowest stage no more than a quarter of full capacity on systems of seventy kilowatts or more and no more than half on systems between twenty-five and seventy kilowatts. The reference building's staged rooftop units previously followed only the equal-increment staging rule, whose increment can leave a two- or three-stage unit in the seventy-to-two-hundred-kilowatt range with a lowest stage above the prescribed fraction. Staged cooling coils on loops that carry an air economizer now take a stage-count floor equal to the reciprocal of the prescribed fraction, raised above the incremental count when necessary and audited whenever the floor governs; every loop the floor can reach is above the economizer retention threshold, so the build-time economizer state is decisive and no reordering of the pipeline was needed. The sentence permitting outdoor-air reduction at the lowest stage is a permission rather than a requirement and is not exercised, because the staged supply-flow ratios are already floored at the minimum outdoor-air fraction. A four-stage unit with an economizer was gated through a clean simulation before the change landed, and the economizer coverage entry graduates from partial to implemented, its last declared gap closed.

decisions.title: The NECB 2025 edition's tables are verified against the printed code: efficiencies re-checked post-extraction-fix, selection verbatim 2020
decisions.summary: The same verification pass that checked the 2020 equipment-efficiency data against the printed tables was run for the 2025 edition, whose vendored file had been transcribed before the table-extraction service was fixed and carried a letter map from the corrupted extraction. Re-fetched against the corrected extraction, the 2025 table lettering mirrors 2020 exactly, and the earlier claim that the packaged-terminal table had changed - which had left the carried-over coefficients under suspicion - turns out to have been an artifact of reading the wrong table: the packaged-terminal table is identical in both printed editions, so the applied coefficients are correct. The chiller, boiler and heat-rejection tables are likewise identical across editions and are pinned to stay identical in the vendored data. The genuine 2025 changes are confined to the small air-conditioner and heat-pump bins: the split-system seasonal heating factor rises, new single-phase rows appear under the updated testing procedure - vendored but inert, since their subcategory never matches the engine's lookup - and the small heat-pump cooling bin takes the printed table's seasonal rating where the 2020 file keeps the legacy full-load reading, a documented cross-edition interpretation difference that is nearly inert because the shared-unit reference rooftop almost always sizes into the larger bins, which match exactly in both editions. The reference-system selection table of the 2025 edition is verbatim the 2020 table, the vendored selection rules differ only in table-number strings, and the full catalog matrix run under the 2025 vintage produces assignments identical to the adjudicated 2020 golden.

decisions.title: The vendored NECB 2020 equipment-efficiency minimums are verified against the printed tables
decisions.summary: Every equipment-efficiency family the reference path applies was compared value-by-value against the printed minimum-performance tables retrieved from the code service. The unitary air-conditioner ladder, the packaged-terminal formula (whose printed per-kilowatt coefficient reappears exactly as the vendored per-kBtu-per-hour one), the heat-pump heating ladder, the boiler ladder and the furnace rows all match their printed cells, the furnace and small-heat-pump rows through documented row-choice interpretations: the small cooling bin takes the single-package-vertical EER rather than the residential seasonal rating, a lenient-side reading that is nearly inert because the shared-unit reference rooftop almost always sizes into the exactly-matching larger bins. The chiller ladder, which carried no provenance at all, turns out to be the printed chiller table's PATH B full-load coefficients of performance converted precisely to kilowatts per ton - the compliance path election is now documented rather than implicit, with the vendored reference part-load curves standing in for the path's integrated part-load requirement since the simulation carries a full-load rating plus curves, not an IPLV. The heat-rejection family cites ASHRAE 90.1 vintages rather than the NECB, but is VESTIGIAL: the reference path never reads it, because the reference cooling tower's fan power is set from the fan-power table and the tower-cell rules instead. Each verified value is pinned by a test that states the printed number and the conversion reaching the vendored one, so a future data regeneration that drifts from the code text fails with the printed value in the message. The 2025 edition's air-conditioner and heat-pump families differ from 2020's and await the same pass.

decisions.title: Residential compatible-cooling and heat-pump detection are decided from facts, not family names
decisions.summary: A verification matrix that built every catalog system as a proposed building and checked the reference assignment it produced against the printed selection table exposed three ways name-based tests got the code wrong, all now decided from characterized facts instead. First, the residential rule that makes the reference identical to a proposed cooled by packaged terminal units, room air conditioners or fan coils matched only catalog family strings, so legacy-named and foreign buildings - including the validated fleet's own hotel guest blocks, whose zones are cooled by packaged terminal air conditioners named verbatim in the table - were sent to through-the-wall systems instead of the copy the table requires; the test now reads the actual zonal cooling units and the loop's own direct-expansion cooling. Second, a heat pump that supplies conditioned water to a hydronic loop - a central plant heat pump serving fan coils or baseboards - was invisible to the redirect that sends heat-pump blocks to the air-source heat-pump reference, because detection stopped at coil level; the serving plant's heat pump now marks the group, and the plant's source loop is classified by the same boundary evidence used for water-to-air units. Third, a district-energy object standing in for a ground field on a heat pump's source loop was read as purchased heating, which routed the reference to the gas-fired purchased-energy representation; source loops of plant heat pumps are now excluded from purchased-energy detection, so a ground-source heat-pump proposed gets the air-source heat-pump reference the heat-pump article prescribes rather than a gas system.

decisions.title: Service water heater part-load curve carries the code fuel-ratio curve transformed into the EnergyPlus part-load-factor domain
decisions.summary: The code states the reference fuel-fired water heater's part-load behaviour as a quadratic ratio of design fuel consumption, whereas the simulation engine's part-load-factor field is an efficiency divisor, so the two express the same requirement in different domains and cannot be compared coefficient by coefficient. The vendored cubic is the polynomial image of that transform and is verified functionally against the code curve on a sampled part-load range rather than by its coefficients; entering the code's own quadratic into the engine field would invert the relation, roughly double part-load fuel at half load, and double-count standby the engine already models separately. The curve is applied to gas- and oil-fired heaters, storage and instantaneous alike, and is withheld from electric heaters because the governing article covers only fuel-fired equipment, a scope limit that is audited rather than left as a silent skip.

decisions.title: The proposed's demand-control ventilation strategy is carried across the reference teardown, but its peak-rate outdoor-air method is not
decisions.summary: The reference building is required to be modelled with the same demand-control ventilation strategies the proposed building implements, but the reference air systems are rebuilt from scratch and their fresh outdoor-air controllers start with demand control switched off, so a proposed building with demand control was being compared against a reference that ventilated at full design rate whenever its fans ran. The characterization step now records each proposed air loop's demand-control setting before the old systems are torn out, and the rebuilt reference controllers receive the same setting. The simulation engine states demand control as a flag plus an outdoor-air method, and only the methods that are themselves demand-control schemes — carbon-dioxide sensing and occupancy-proportional control — are copied, because the remaining methods determine the PEAK ventilation rate, which a different sentence governs and which the reference already inherits from the cloned space ventilation specifications.

decisions.title: Reference humidification is rebuilt on the proposed's energy source with a control taken from the proposed, or it is not built at all
decisions.summary: The reference building's humidification is required to use the same energy source as the corresponding humidification in the proposed building, which presupposes the reference carries humidification wherever the proposed does. Previously the humidifiers were merely counted before the old systems were torn out and one warning was issued, which both misreported systems that were never replaced and let the rest be destroyed as an unintended side effect. Each thermal block's humidification is now recorded before the teardown and re-created on the serving reference air system as the same steam-humidifier type — electric resistance or gas-fired — with its capacity left to the sizing run. The humidity control is taken from the proposed building rather than invented: the zone humidistat that survives on the thermal zone, or failing that the proposed system's own scheduled minimum-humidity setpoint; where neither exists no humidifier is built, because a humidifier without a setpoint never operates and would falsely present the reference as humidified.

decisions.title: Reference fan-coil systems get a real water-side economizer, and the cooling-tower setpoint reset is what makes it operate
decisions.summary: The reference selection table sends the fan-coil systems to the indirect, water-side form of cooling with outdoor air rather than to the air-side economizer, and that requirement was previously only warned about, leaving the reference with no economizer at all while the quality-assurance checker flagged the same system for lacking one. A plate heat exchanger is now built between the heat-rejection loop and the chilled-water loop, sized from the loop's full design cooling load and modulating onto the chilled-water loop's own design supply temperature. Because the reference rejects heat through an evaporative cooling tower, the wet-bulb criterion is the sentence that governs and the sensible-transfer criterion is recorded as inapplicable; the tower setpoint must also be reset to track the outdoor wet-bulb plus the tower's design approach, since the builder otherwise pins the loop at its design heat-rejection temperature and no exchanger placed there could ever operate.

decisions.title: Reference daylighting photocontrols follow the current daylight-responsive control requirement, not the superseded one
decisions.summary: Where the reference building must carry daylight-responsive photocontrols is now decided by the current requirement rather than by criteria carried over from a superseded edition of the code. The current requirement gates each space type through the prescriptive lighting-control table, then tests the input power of the general lighting inside the daylighted areas against fixed wattage thresholds - one for the primary sidelighted areas, a higher one for primary plus secondary, and a separate one for the areas under skylights - and treats the sidelighting and toplighting requirements as INDEPENDENT of one another. The superseded criteria were area and effective-aperture tests applied conjunctively, so a space lit only by windows failed on its zero skylight area and never received photocontrols at all, which left the reference building carrying fewer controls than the code requires and therefore set an energy target more lenient than the code writes. Because the lighting power density is uniform across each space, the input power inside a daylighted area is exactly the density times that area, so no luminaire layout is needed. The daylighted areas themselves are now built as unioned polygons so overlapping areas are not double-counted, a secondary sidelighted area is computed at all, and the code's own precedence - a primary sidelighted area is never reduced by a skylight, while a secondary area yields to both - is applied. The published exceptions are honoured, including the exemption of retail spaces from the sidelighting requirement and of low-transmittance skylights and high-latitude buildings with little lighting power from the toplighting requirement. Two independent extractions of the prescriptive control table are each partly corrupted and disagree with one another, so the vendored control matrix records a state per space type rather than a bare flag: columns that cannot be read are warned about and take a documented conservative default that tightens rather than loosens the target, and space types the table does not list at all are determined from the code text to fall outside the requirement instead of being guessed at. The superseded rule remains selectable so that the parity gate against the legacy implementation stays callable, and selecting it warns that the resulting target is looser than the code requires.

decisions.title: CBECS evap-cooler values aligned to legacy (two unsourced deviations closed)
decisions.summary: The evap-cooler builder's design effectiveness and supply setpoint-manager offset and clamps were the only builder values that both differed from the legacy implementation and had no traced source. Both now mirror legacy exactly: effectiveness 0.90 per the PNNL-cited legacy value, and a wet-bulb-following supply setpoint at a 3 Rankine approach clamped between 70 and 78 Fahrenheit, converted through the same SDK calls the legacy code uses so the resulting fields are bit-identical. This is a CBECS-only family that no NECB archetype builds, and no audit entry cites this id because the builder logs no entries for these fields.

decisions.title: Clarity restructure: aliased public renames + the openstudio-audit gem
decisions.summary: The restructure pass renamed four public surfaces with back-compat aliases - the reference-ASHP catalog marker (heat_source ashp, replacing a DX heating-coil misnomer), the geometry facade's storeys vocabulary, the single daylighting placement selector with option as a deprecated alias, and the extraction of the shared audit log and coverage emitter into the openstudio-audit gem, retiring six synchronized copies. Every rename was proof-gated: canonical names and built model objects byte-identical, the selection golden green including the full matrix, and the coverage-emitter unification shown behavior-neutral by an empty before-and-after citation-count diff.
